# Using libtmux for Haskell

Capture a tmux server once, then use the records as ordinary Haskell. Start
with the [capture program](../README.md), then [capture and recovery](capture.md)
and the [API guide](api.md).

| Task | Guide |
| --- | --- |
| Add the source package to a Cabal application | [Installation](installation.md) |
| Capture, filter and traverse the object graph | [Observations and recovery](capture.md) |
| Inspect typed selections and check physical or contextual uniqueness | [Typed queries](query.md) |
| Create a session and operate on its returned references | [Session creation](creation.md) |
| Run a terminal application, send input and clean up its scope | [Owned programs](programs.md) |
| Rename captured targets and handle interrupted commands | [Mutations and recovery](mutations.md) |
| Share resources across independent Server scopes | [Shared Runtime](shared-runtime.md) |
| Test application predicates without tmux | [Validated offline fixtures](fixtures.md) |
| Reproduce capture measurements | [Performance](performance.md) |
| Parse IDs, validate geometry and admit a release | [Typed values](values.md) |
| Browse modules, declarations and source | [API documentation](api.md) |
| Decide whether the current package meets your needs | [Implementation status](status.md) |

For maintainers:

- [Behavior contracts](contracts/README.md): implementation scope, including
  operations that are not public APIs yet.
- [Native domain model ADR](decisions/0001-native-domain-model.md): physical
  graph, naming, lifecycle and public API decisions.
- [Contributing](../.github/CONTRIBUTING.md) and
  [testing](../.github/TESTING.md): setup and test authoring.

# Add the package to a Cabal application

Requirements:

- A current GHC and Cabal, within the bounds in the
  [package manifest](../libtmux-haskell.cabal).
- Linux x86_64; see [host requirements](#native-backend-host-requirements).
- tmux 3.3a or newer.
- To reproduce the tested toolchain, see
  [contributor setup](../.github/CONTRIBUTING.md#toolchain).

Add `libtmux-haskell` to your executable's dependencies and
[fetch the Git source](#fetch-the-source-from-git) with a `cabal.project`.
The [example package](../examples/capture-graph/libtmux-capture-graph.cabal) is
a complete starting point:

<!-- example-package: capture-graph -->
```cabal
cabal-version: 3.18
name: libtmux-capture-graph
version: 0.0.0
build-type: Simple
license: MIT
extra-doc-files: README.md

executable capture-graph
  main-is: Main.hs
  default-language: GHC2024
  ghc-options: -Wall -Werror
  build-depends:
    base >=4.22 && <4.23,
    filepath >=1.5.4 && <1.6,
    libtmux-haskell ^>=0.0.1.0,
    text >=2.1.3 && <2.2
```

Save [Main.hs](../examples/capture-graph/Main.hs) beside the package file, then
update the package index:

```console
$ cabal update
```

Start the [demo server](../README.md) from the README, then run:

```console
$ cabal run --verbose=0 capture-graph -- \
    "$LIBTMUX_DEMO_DIR/s" \
    "$(command -v tmux)"
```

- Enable
  [`OverloadedRecordDot`](https://downloads.haskell.org/ghc/latest/docs/users_guide/exts/overloaded_record_dot.html)
  in modules that read observation fields.
- No optics or effect framework is needed.
- The [capture guide](capture.md) covers the object graph, pure lookups and
  scope cleanup.

The API is experimental. The package provides observation, rename/title
and existing-server session creation operations, plus scoped terminal programs
with input, rendered output and exit observation. Program needs tmux 3.8,
Linux 6.9 process-group pidfds and the Bash features described in the
[program guide](programs.md). First-server bootstrap, general window/pane
commands and byte streaming remain under development.
Check [status](status.md) before choosing it for automation.

Browse the [manual](https://libtmux.org/en/haskell/) and
[`LibTmux.Server` API](https://libtmux.org/en/haskell/latest/reference/libtmux-server/)
for connection, capture and mutation operations.

## Fetch the source from Git

The package is not on Hackage yet, so Cabal fetches a source revision from Git.
Use this `cabal.project`:

<!-- example-project: capture-graph -->
```cabal
packages: .
index-state: 2026-11-06T00:00:00Z

source-repository-package
  type: git
  location: https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-haskell
  tag: 8593bef1754e4048b40b753e446da0f90848191f
```

## Native backend host requirements

The native backend needs:

- Linux x86_64.
- glibc 2.39 or newer, for `pidfd_spawn`.
- A kernel with compatible pidfd operations.
- Exclusive ownership of child reaping.

A missing host operation fails before launch. Pure scalar construction and
lookup do not need them. See the
[process host contract](contracts/process.md#launch-and-host-requirements).

# Capture and navigate a tmux server

[`withServer`](../src/LibTmux/Server.hs) adopts an existing tmux endpoint.
[`capture`](../src/LibTmux/Server.hs) reads it into a detached
[`Snapshot`](../src/LibTmux/Snapshot.hs) that stays usable after the handle
closes. The [README](../README.md) shows the
[complete program](../examples/capture-graph/Main.hs).

Start the [demo server](../README.md) from the README, then run from a
checkout:

```console
$ cabal run --verbose=0 capture-graph -- \
    "$LIBTMUX_DEMO_DIR/s" \
    "$(command -v tmux)"
```

To inspect your own server, pass its socket and tmux executable instead. The
program reads that daemon; it never creates or stops it.

The library needs:

- A trusted absolute socket path.
- A writable pin directory on the socket's filesystem. The default is the
  socket's parent.
- A Linux host; see [installation](installation.md#native-backend-host-requirements).

## Physical entities and appearances

A session links windows at numeric indices. One physical window can appear at
two indices, or in several sessions. A pane belongs to its physical window; a
pane occurrence also keeps the window-link context:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    S["Session demo"] --> L0["WindowLink index 0"]
    S --> L4["WindowLink index 4"]
    L0 --> W["Window @0"]
    L4 --> W
    W --> P["Pane %0"]
```

- `windows` and `panes` return each physical entity once.
- `windowLinks` and `paneOccurrences` return every appearance: two each in
  this demo.
- Order: lists by numeric ID; links by session ID, then window index;
  occurrences by link, then pane index. Lookups are indexed.

References:

- A reference names a target within one Server generation. Independent Server
  scopes have distinct generations.
- A lookup returns the observation in the snapshot you pass, including a later
  capture from the same Server.
- `lookupPaneId` picks a native ID's observation in the snapshot you pass. It
  does not restore an earlier targeting guarantee.

Values:

- Record updates make local values. They do not change the snapshot's indexes,
  validate the edited graph or send a command.
- Compare sizes with `dimensionValue pane.width`; dimensions have no
  [`Num`](https://hackage-content.haskell.org/package/base-4.22.0.0/docs/Prelude.html#t:Num)
  instance.
- Paths and command names keep POSIX bytes. Window labels are `TmuxText`;
  converting to text is explicit and can fail.

## Errors and recovery

- Acquisition fails in `IO` with `TmuxException`.
- Pure navigation returns `Either LookupError`. A missing or foreign reference
  is never an empty result.
- A snapshot records a monotonic capture interval. It is not a transaction over
  tmux and operating-system state.

`withServer` rethrows the callback's own exception, cancellation included.

- If bounded cleanup stays incomplete, the exception context holds a
  `CleanupRecovery`.
- After a successful callback, incomplete cleanup raises `CleanupFailed`.

Catch with:

- `tryTmux`: library failures.
- [`Control.Exception.tryWithContext`](https://hackage-content.haskell.org/package/base-4.22.0.0/docs/Control-Exception.html#v:tryWithContext):
  also application exceptions and cancellation.

Both keep the
[`ExceptionWithContext`](https://hackage-content.haskell.org/package/base-4.22.0.0/docs/Control-Exception.html#t:ExceptionWithContext)
that recovery needs. A typed `try` drops it.

`cleanupRecoveries` and `captureRecoveries` read the correlated owners from
that context. For each owner you can:

- Inspect it locally.
- Resume cleanup. This never sends a second capture.
- Detach the uncertainty. This stops no native resource and proves nothing
  about the daemon.

Details: [process contract](contracts/process.md).

## See also

- [Offline fixtures](fixtures.md): test graph logic without tmux.
- [Performance](performance.md): capture cost by graph size.
- [Shared Runtime](shared-runtime.md): independent handle lifetimes.
- [Status](status.md): what is implemented.

# Select observations with typed queries

[`runQuery`](../src/LibTmux/Query.hs) evaluates a typed query over a
[`Snapshot`](../src/LibTmux/Snapshot.hs) and returns lists in
`Either QueryError`. Use it when you need to inspect a predicate, use typed
fields or compose relationships. Plain comprehensions and `filter` still work
for everything else; see [capture](capture.md).

The program finds active panes at least 120 cells wide, then:

- Compares the query with a plain predicate on one snapshot.
- Checks uniqueness.
- Follows session, link and pane relationships.
- Prints the fields the query requires.

The demo links one window at indices 0 and 4, so its one physical pane
appears twice as a contextual match.

Start the [demo server](../README.md) from the README, then run from a
[checkout](../.github/CONTRIBUTING.md#toolchain):

```console
$ cabal run --verbose=0 query-graph -- \
    "$LIBTMUX_DEMO_DIR/s" \
    "$(command -v tmux)"
```

Everything in it is pure except [`capture`](../src/LibTmux/Server.hs) and
[`fetch`](../src/LibTmux/Query.hs).

<!-- example: query-graph -->
```haskell
{-# LANGUAGE OverloadedRecordDot #-}
{-# LANGUAGE OverloadedStrings #-}

-- | Query one detached graph, then distinguish physical and contextual matches.
module Main (main) where

import Control.Exception (ExceptionWithContext, rethrowIO)
import Data.Bifunctor (first)
import Data.Function ((&))
import Data.Text qualified as Text
import LibTmux qualified as Tmux
import LibTmux.Query qualified as Q
import LibTmux.Query.Link qualified as Link
import LibTmux.Query.Occurrence qualified as Occurrence
import LibTmux.Query.Pane qualified as Pane
import LibTmux.Query.Session qualified as Session
import System.Environment (getArgs)
import System.Exit (die)
import System.OsPath.Posix qualified as Path

data ApplicationError
  = OperationalFailure (ExceptionWithContext Tmux.TmuxException)
  | InvalidQuery Q.QueryError
  | InvalidSelection Q.CardinalityError
  | UnexpectedResult String

activeWide :: Q.Expr Tmux.Pane
activeWide = Q.allOf [Q.eq Pane.active True, Q.dimensionAtLeast Pane.width 120]

selectedPanes :: Q.Query Tmux.Pane
selectedPanes = Q.panes & Q.matching activeWide

main :: IO ()
main = getArgs >>= \case
  [socketArgument, executableArgument] -> do
    socket <- Path.encodeFS socketArgument
    executable <- Path.encodeFS executableArgument
    let config = (Tmux.serverConfig socket) {Tmux.executable = executable}
    acquired <- Tmux.tryTmux $ Tmux.withServer config $ \server -> do
      snapshot <- Tmux.capture server
      fresh <- Q.fetch server selectedPanes
      pure (snapshot, fresh)
    case first OperationalFailure acquired >>= uncurry report of
      Left (OperationalFailure problem) -> rethrowIO problem
      Left (InvalidQuery problem) -> die ("Query validation failed: " <> show problem)
      Left (InvalidSelection problem) -> die ("Selection failed: " <> show problem)
      Left (UnexpectedResult problem) -> die problem
      Right linesToPrint -> mapM_ putStrLn linesToPrint
  _ -> die "Usage: query-graph SOCKET TMUX_EXECUTABLE"

report :: Tmux.Snapshot -> Either Q.QueryError [Tmux.Pane] -> Either ApplicationError [String]
report snapshot acquired = do
  selected <- first InvalidQuery (Q.runQuery snapshot selectedPanes)
  let native = [pane | pane <- Tmux.panes snapshot, pane.active, Tmux.dimensionValue pane.width >= 120]
  if selected == native then Right () else Left (UnexpectedResult "query and native selection disagree")
  unique <- first InvalidSelection (Q.exactlyOne selected)
  occurrences <- first InvalidQuery $ Q.runQuery snapshot $
    Q.paneOccurrences & Q.matching (Q.related Occurrence.pane activeWide)
  highest <- first InvalidQuery $ Q.runQuery snapshot $
    Q.windowLinks & Q.orderBy [Q.descending Link.index] & Q.limit 1
  link <- first InvalidSelection (Q.exactlyOne highest)
  let containingEditors = Q.sessions & Q.matching (Q.some Session.windowLinks (Q.some Link.panes activeWide))
  sessions <- first InvalidQuery (Q.runQuery snapshot containingEditors)
  fresh <- first InvalidQuery acquired
  Right
    [ "query agrees with native predicate: True"
    , "unique physical pane: " <> Text.unpack (Tmux.renderPaneId (Tmux.paneId unique.ref))
    , "contextual matches: " <> show (length occurrences)
    , "contextual uniqueness: " <> either show (const "unique") (Q.exactlyOne occurrences)
    , "highest link index: " <> show (Tmux.windowIndexValue link.index)
    , "sessions containing a match: " <> show (length sessions)
    , "required fields: " <> show (Q.requirements selectedPanes).fieldNames
    , "required relationships: " <> show (Q.requirements containingEditors).relationshipNames
    , "fresh capture matches: " <> show (length fresh)
    ]
```

Expected output:

<!-- example-output: query-graph -->
```text
query agrees with native predicate: True
unique physical pane: %0
contextual matches: 2
contextual uniqueness: AtLeastTwoMatches
highest link index: 4
sessions containing a match: 1
required fields: ["pane.active","pane.width"]
required relationships: ["session.windowLinks","windowLink.panes"]
fresh capture matches: 1
```

## Choose the source before checking cardinality

- [`panes`](../src/LibTmux/Query.hs) selects unique physical panes.
- [`paneOccurrences`](../src/LibTmux/Query.hs) selects their appearances
  through window links. Filtering keeps the source's multiplicity.
- `exactlyOne` rejects no match and reports `AtLeastTwoMatches` at the second
  match, without counting the rest. Proving uniqueness can still traverse every
  input element.
- `atMostOne` also allows no match.

Relationships:

- [`some`](../src/LibTmux/Query.hs) tests one related child against its whole
  predicate. To require several conditions on one pane, put them all inside it;
  two separate `some` predicates can match different panes.
- On a known empty relation, `some` is false; `every` and `none` are true.
- `optionalRelated` is false for a known absent target. Its negation includes
  absence.
- A missing required lookup is an error. So is an unavailable relationship,
  even on an empty source or in a short-circuited branch.

## Inspect, order and limit

- The qualified [field modules](api.md) expose typed tokens. Boolean fields
  reject numeric comparisons; fields of different row types do not mix.
- `dimensionAtLeast` takes an unbounded `Integer`; observed dimensions keep
  their checked type.
- Text equality and containment are exact: no case folding, no Unicode
  normalization.
- Command names, paths and window labels keep their byte-preserving types,
  with no implicit text conversion.

[`requirements`](../src/LibTmux/Query.hs) lists a query's source, field and
relationship names, ordering keys and limit. It inspects dependencies; it is
not serialization or an execution plan. Validation checks every declared
requirement before reading rows, including ordering keys, empty membership
predicates and zero limits.

Building a query:

- `matching` adds predicates.
- `orderBy` replaces the ordering keys. The sort is stable, so ties keep source
  order.
- `limit` replaces the final bound, a nonnegative `Natural`.
- Evaluation always filters, then orders, then limits, whatever the builder
  order.
- Descriptions and operand lists must be finite.

## Keep acquisition and failures explicit

- [`fetch`](../src/LibTmux/Query.hs) captures a new complete snapshot on every
  call. It checks evaluator support before acquiring, then validates version
  requirements against the captured metadata.
- It does no backend filtering. To share observations across selections, reuse
  `runQuery` on one snapshot; see [capture costs](performance.md).

Errors:

- The example folds operational, query and cardinality errors into one
  application error type.
- `tryTmux` catches library exceptions only; asynchronous cancellation
  propagates.
- `rethrowIO` keeps the exception context, so cleanup and capture recovery
  owners stay reachable. To inspect and resume them, see
  [recovery](capture.md).

Reading the result:

- The report reads detached values after the Server closes.
- The equality check uses one snapshot; the fresh-capture count is a second
  acquisition. Two captures of a changing server do not prove the evaluator
  equals the plain predicate.
- Cardinality and reference equality describe what was observed, not what is
  alive now.
- Query interchange, backend optimization and event streams are not
  implemented; see [status](status.md).

To use it in your own application, copy the
[program](../examples/query-graph/Main.hs) and
[package file](../examples/query-graph/libtmux-query-graph.cabal), then add its
[pinned source dependency](../examples/query-graph/cabal.project.vcs) as
described in [installation](installation.md).

# Create sessions, windows and panes

[`createSession`](../src/LibTmux/Server.hs) creates a detached session through
an existing [`Server`](../src/LibTmux/Server.hs). It returns the actual session,
initial window and pane references printed by tmux. Use those references for
commands, then capture again to observe the resulting graph.
[`createWindow` and `splitPane`](../src/LibTmux/Server.hs) use the same historical
receipts and recovery path with explicit placement and pane targets.

Start the [README's private demonstration server](../README.md), then run
from a [provisioned checkout](../.github/CONTRIBUTING.md#toolchain):

```console
$ cabal run --verbose=0 create-session -- \
    "$LIBTMUX_DEMO_DIR/s" \
    "$(command -v tmux)"
```

The program checks an empty value, a removal marker and an absent entry
in the new session's [environment](mutations.md#read-and-change-the-environment).
It adds a window and splits an explicit pane, then links that window
at a second index, selects an exact pane, tiles the window and removes the
extra link. The new pane disables terminal echo, prints a readiness marker and starts `/bin/cat -`.
The caller waits for the marker and [captures a baseline](mutations.md#read-pane-text).
It [sends literal text and a named Enter](mutations.md#send-input-to-a-pane),
then [waits for fresh text](mutations.md#wait-for-pane-text) from the pane.
The program checks duplicate-name rejection, removes its targets and verifies
that the original sessions survive. Captures remain readable after the handle
closes. Follow the [README's teardown](../README.md#clean-up)
for the borrowed demonstration server.

<!-- example: create-session -->
```haskell
{-# LANGUAGE OverloadedRecordDot #-}
{-# LANGUAGE OverloadedStrings #-}

-- | Create native targets, refresh their graph, and retain detached values.
module Main (main) where

import Control.Exception (ExceptionWithContext (..), rethrowIO)
import Control.Monad (unless)
import Data.List.NonEmpty (NonEmpty (..))
import Data.Text qualified as Text
import LibTmux qualified as Tmux
import LibTmux.Creation qualified as Creation
import System.Environment (getArgs)
import System.Exit (die)
import System.OsPath.Posix qualified as Path
import System.OsString.Posix qualified as Os

main :: IO ()
main = getArgs >>= \case
  [socketArgument, executableArgument] -> do
    socket <- Path.encodeFS socketArgument
    executable <- Path.encodeFS executableArgument
    width <- require "Width" (Tmux.mkDimension 120)
    extraIndex <- require "Second link index" (Tmux.mkWindowIndex 4)
    let config = (Tmux.serverConfig socket) {Tmux.executable = executable}
        options = Creation.defaultSessionOptions
          { Creation.name = Just "created-workspace"
          , Creation.windowName = Just (Tmux.labelFromBytes "editor")
          , Creation.width = Just width
          , Creation.process = Creation.DirectCommand (Os.fromBytestring "/bin/cat") (Os.fromBytestring "-" :| [])
          }
    result <- Tmux.tryTmux $ Tmux.withServer config $ \server -> do
      before <- Tmux.capture server
      created <- Tmux.createSession server options
      let environment = Tmux.SessionEnvironment created.session
          key = "LIBTMUX_EXAMPLE_STATE"
      Tmux.setEnvironment server environment key Tmux.Visible ""
      empty <- Tmux.getEnvironment server environment key
      Tmux.markEnvironmentRemoved server environment key
      removed <- Tmux.getEnvironment server environment key
      Tmux.unsetEnvironment server environment key
      absent <- Tmux.getEnvironment server environment key
      unless (empty == Just (Tmux.EnvironmentValue Tmux.Visible "")
          && removed == Just (Tmux.EnvironmentRemoved Tmux.Visible) && absent == Nothing)
        (die "Expected distinct empty, removed and absent entries")
      Tmux.renameWindow server created.window "api"
      Tmux.setPaneTitle server created.pane "editor-ready"
      added <- Tmux.createWindow server (Creation.NextFree created.session)
        Creation.defaultWindowOptions {Creation.windowLabel = Just "worker", Creation.windowProcess = options.process}
      let workerSlot = Creation.WindowSlot added.session added.windowIndex
          secondLink = Creation.WindowSlot added.session extraIndex
      split <- Tmux.splitPane server workerSlot added.pane
        Creation.defaultSplitOptions
          { Creation.direction = Creation.LeftRight
          , Creation.size = Creation.SplitPercent 25
          , Creation.splitProcess = Creation.ShellCommand
              "stty -echo; printf 'input-ready\\n'; exec /bin/cat -"
          }
      Tmux.linkWindow server workerSlot secondLink
      Tmux.selectWindowLink server secondLink
      Tmux.selectExactPane server secondLink split.pane
      Tmux.selectLayout server secondLink Tmux.Tiled
      linked <- Tmux.capture server
      linkedSlots <- require "Worker links" (Tmux.linksForSession linked added.session)
      let workerIndices = [Tmux.windowIndexValue link.index | link <- linkedSlots, link.window == added.window]
      Tmux.unlinkWindow server secondLink
      _ <- awaitText server split.pane Tmux.defaultPaneWait "input-ready"
      baseline <- Tmux.capturePane server split.pane Tmux.defaultPaneCapture
      Tmux.sendKeys server split.pane (Tmux.LiteralText "Enter")
      Tmux.sendKeys server split.pane (Tmux.NamedKeys ("Enter" :| []))
      screen <- awaitText server split.pane
        Tmux.defaultPaneWait {Tmux.waitMatch = Tmux.FreshSince baseline} "Enter"
      after <- Tmux.capture server
      duplicate <- Tmux.tryTmux (Tmux.createSession server options)
      rejected <- case duplicate of
        Left (ExceptionWithContext _ (Tmux.MutationRejected _)) -> pure True
        Left problem -> rethrowIO problem
        Right _ -> die "Duplicate creation unexpectedly succeeded"
      Tmux.killSession server created.session
      let disposable = options {Creation.name = Nothing}
      windowOwner <- Tmux.createSession server disposable
      Tmux.killWindow server windowOwner.window
      paneOwner <- Tmux.createSession server disposable
      Tmux.killPane server paneOwner.pane
      remaining <- Tmux.capture server
      pure (created, added, split, before, after, screen, workerIndices, rejected, remaining)
    case result of
      Left problem -> rethrowIO problem
      Right (created, added, split, before, after, screen, workerIndices, rejected, remaining) -> do
        session <- require "Created session" (Tmux.lookupSession after created.session)
        window <- require "Created window" (Tmux.lookupWindow after created.window)
        pane <- require "Created pane" (Tmux.lookupPane after created.pane)
        worker <- require "New window" (Tmux.lookupWindow after added.window)
        panes <- require "New window panes" (Tmux.panesForWindow after added.window)
        splitPane <- require "Split pane" (Tmux.lookupPane after split.pane)
        links <- require "Created session links" (Tmux.linksForSession after created.session)
        label <- require "Window label" (Tmux.labelText window.name)
        workerLabel <- require "New window label" (Tmux.labelText worker.name)
        putStrLn $ "created session: " <> Text.unpack session.name
        putStrLn "session environment: empty, removed, absent"
        putStrLn $ "initial window: " <> Text.unpack label
        putStrLn $ "pane title: " <> Text.unpack pane.title
        putStrLn $ "same created targets: " <> show (session.ref == created.session && window.ref == created.window && pane.ref == created.pane)
        putStrLn $ "captured sessions: " <> show (length (Tmux.sessions before)) <> " -> " <> show (length (Tmux.sessions after))
        putStrLn $ "created session links: " <> show (length links)
        putStrLn $ "new window: " <> Text.unpack workerLabel
        putStrLn $ "new window panes: " <> show (length panes)
        putStrLn $ "same worker window at indices: " <> show workerIndices
        putStrLn $ "split exact target: " <> show (splitPane.window == added.window && split.session == added.session && split.windowIndex == added.windowIndex)
        putStrLn $ "captured pane rows match height: " <> show
          (toInteger (length (Text.lines (Tmux.paneText screen))) == Tmux.dimensionValue splitPane.height)
        putStrLn "captured pane text"
        putStr (Text.unpack (Text.unlines (filter (not . Text.null) (Text.lines (Tmux.paneText screen)))))
        putStrLn $ "duplicate name rejected: " <> show rejected
        putStrLn $ "original sessions after removal: " <> show
          (map (.ref) (Tmux.sessions remaining) == map (.ref) (Tmux.sessions before))
  _ -> die "Usage: create-session SOCKET TMUX_EXECUTABLE"

awaitText :: Tmux.Server -> Tmux.PaneRef -> Tmux.PaneWaitOptions -> Text.Text -> IO Tmux.PaneText
awaitText server pane options expected =
  Tmux.waitForText server pane options expected >>= \case
    Tmux.PaneTextMatched screen -> pure screen
    Tmux.PaneTextTimedOut _ _ -> die "Timed out waiting for pane text"
    Tmux.PaneTextExited _ -> die "Pane exited before producing text"

require :: Show problem => String -> Either problem a -> IO a
require context = either (die . ((context <> ": ") <>) . show) pure
```

## Link, select and arrange windows

[`linkWindow`](../src/LibTmux/Server.hs) takes a source slot and a vacant
destination slot. The new slot points to the same physical window and starts
unselected. Use [`selectWindowLink`](../src/LibTmux/Server.hs) to activate a
specific session/index, even when the same window appears at two indices.

[`selectExactPane`](../src/LibTmux/Server.hs) takes a window slot and an exact
pane reference. The pane must belong to that slot's current window.
[`selectLayout`](../src/LibTmux/Server.hs) applies one of the five layout names
shared by tmux 3.3a and 3.8. It affects the physical window seen through every
link and can unzoom it. Capture again to read the active pane and geometry.

[`unlinkWindow`](../src/LibTmux/Server.hs) removes only the named link and
refuses to remove the last one. Native session groups can propagate link
changes to their members. Use the `With` variants for explicit deadlines.

## Remove a target

Use [`killSession`](../src/LibTmux/Server.hs) for a session,
[`killWindow`](../src/LibTmux/Server.hs) for a physical window and all its
links, and [`killPane`](../src/LibTmux/Server.hs) for a pane. tmux closes a
window when its last pane is removed, and a session when its last window
closes. Capture again to see what remains.

The `With` variants take [`MutationOptions`](../src/LibTmux/Server.hs).
A missing native target fails with `MutationRejected`. A foreign or offline
reference fails with `InvalidTarget` before dispatch. Command completion
confirms the removal response. Observe descendant process exit separately.

## Options and process modes

Start from [`defaultSessionOptions`](../src/LibTmux/Creation.hs). Import
`LibTmux.Creation` qualified for option updates, as the program does; several
observation types also have fields named `name`, `width` and `height`.

Session and window names and the working directory stay literal through tmux
format parsing. Checked dimensions must fit the native command's range.
Environment entries override session variables; tmux's configured inheritance
and `update-environment` rules still apply. Relative paths use the calling
client's working directory. The library captures that OS context in `IO` as
part of the command deadline. Options omit
[`Show`](https://hackage.haskell.org/package/base/docs/Prelude.html#t:Show)
because argv and environment values can contain credentials.

[`InitialProcess`](../src/LibTmux/Creation.hs) distinguishes native modes:

- `DefaultProcess` uses tmux's configured default command or default shell.
- `ShellCommand` passes command bytes to tmux's native creation handler. Session
  creation runs even an empty script through the default shell. An empty split
  command instead follows tmux's processless-pane behavior.
- `DirectCommand` executes the program with a nonempty list of arguments.
  tmux treats a single argv entry as shell input, so the type requires at
  least one argument after the executable.

There is no processless session mode. The ordinary creation operation also
requires an existing daemon; it does not bootstrap a first server, reuse an
existing session, attach a terminal or replace a daemon after failure.

## Window placement and pane targets

[`createWindow`](../src/LibTmux/Server.hs) takes a
[`WindowPlacement`](../src/LibTmux/Creation.hs) and `WindowOptions`. Start from
`defaultWindowOptions` and choose `NextFree session`, `At slot`, `Before slot`
or `After slot`. A `WindowSlot session index` means the current occupant of
that position at execution time. It does not freeze a captured window identity.
On a vacant relative slot, tmux creates at that index without shifting links.
`After` refuses index 2147483647 before dispatch because no larger signed
window index exists.

The default `RefuseOccupied` policy reports a native rejection when an exact
slot is occupied. `ReplaceOccupied` removes that link before creating a new
window. Other links can keep the old physical window alive. Insertion can
shift indices and replacement can remove a link before a later failure; neither
mode promises rollback. Session groups can propagate these effects.

`windowLabel` and `windowDirectory` stay literal. Window creation inherits the
target session's geometry; `windowEnvironment` and `splitEnvironment` override
only the new pane's environment. `windowProcess` and `splitProcess` choose its
native initial process.
`selectWindow = True` requests selection in the target session. Replacing its current
link can force selection even when the option is false. Reuse by name remains
outside this API because native reuse can return no creation receipt.

[`splitPane`](../src/LibTmux/Server.hs) takes a `WindowSlot`, an explicit
`PaneRef` and `SplitOptions`. The pane must belong to that slot's physical
window when tmux executes the command. This also distinguishes two indices
linked to the same physical window. A missing pane or changed slot occupant
fails without choosing another active pane.

Start from `defaultSplitOptions`. `LeftRight` splits across columns;
`TopBottom` splits across rows. `before` puts the new pane left or above the
anchor; `fullWindow` spans the perpendicular window dimension. `SplitCells`
and `SplitPercent` request the new pane's extent. Percentages are 1 through 100;
cells and link indices fit tmux's signed 32-bit domain. Native border and
layout constraints can clamp or refuse a requested size. Capture again to
read actual dimensions. `selectPane` requests the new pane as active; `zoom`
zooms the window or keeps it zoomed. Floating-pane extensions remain separate.

## Receipts and fresh observations

[`CreatedEntities`](../src/LibTmux/Creation.hs) is a historical receipt. It contains
opaque references from this Server generation, the execution-time window index
and the daemon PID reported with them. It is not a snapshot or a liveness check.
`CreatedSession`, `CreatedWindow` and `CreatedPane` name the results of each
operation. Only the session command creates all three entities; window creation
retains its existing parent session, and a split retains its existing window.
An after-hook can rename or destroy a target before creation returns. A receipt
also does not prove that the initial process successfully executed or that a
hook's background work finished.

[`capture`](../src/LibTmux/Server.hs) and the indexed
[`lookupSession`, `lookupWindow` and `lookupPane`](../src/LibTmux/Snapshot.hs)
read those identities as observed in the supplied new snapshot. A deleted
target returns a pure lookup error. References from an earlier generation
cannot target a reopened handle. A stale or deleted reference never silently
selects a replacement by name.

## Failure, deadlines and recovery

[`createSessionWith`, `createWindowWith` and `splitPaneWith`](../src/LibTmux/Server.hs)
accept `MutationOptions`.
Its positive timeout, at most ten seconds, covers context acquisition,
admission and the complete command response; the default is one second.
It does not bound the lifetime of the created entities or their processes.

Invalid options raise `InvalidMutationArgument` before admission. Encoded
command arguments fit a 16,364-byte message, including terminators and literal
text escaping. The client invocation also counts toward the argv limit.

The caller's environment shares the native launch budget with argv: at most
4,096 entries and 64 KiB, including paths, terminators and pointer storage.
Exceeding that budget raises `InvalidConfiguration` before admission. Neither
refusal retains a creation operation or includes environment values.

tmux also validates its own input rules and current server state. A duplicate
session name raises
`MutationRejected`; a successful primary creation followed by hook failure
raises `MutationAppliedWithErrors`. Neither failure implies rollback of
independent hook effects. Timeout, cancellation and incomplete responses can
leave the command's outcome unknown. Creation never automatically retries.

[`tryTmux`](../src/LibTmux/Server.hs) preserves library errors and their exception
context. It lets asynchronous cancellation propagate. When catching cancellation
at an application boundary, retain the context from `tryWithContext` too.
Use [`creationRecoveries`](../src/LibTmux/Server.hs) to find the correlated
operation owner rather than searching all Runtime operations.

For each owner, `creationOperation` and `creationGeneration` identify the
request. `creationReceipt` reads any complete IDs already observed without
contacting tmux. [`Nothing`](https://hackage.haskell.org/package/base/docs/Data-Maybe.html#v:Nothing)
does not prove that creation had no effect.
`inspectCreationRecovery` distinguishes logical outcome from native cleanup.
`awaitCreationRecovery` joins the original child and decoder;
`resumeCreationRecovery` resumes existing cleanup. Neither repeats creation.

If logical uncertainty remains, `detachCreationRecovery` explicitly relinquishes
that responsibility while preserving physical cleanup owners. It does not kill
the created entities. Handle any scope-level cleanup owners separately through
[`cleanupRecoveries`](../src/LibTmux/Server.hs). The
[shared Runtime guide](shared-runtime.md) explains ownership across handles;
the [mutation guide](mutations.md) describes the common outcome vocabulary.

# Run a terminal application

[`runProgram`](../src/LibTmux/Server.hs) returns an exact leader outcome and a
bounded rendered screen after cleaning up its owned session. The selected
daemon stays borrowed. Existing sessions, panes and buffers survive.

[`withProgram`](../src/LibTmux/Server.hs) supplies an interactive
[`Program`](../src/LibTmux/Program.hs) inside a scope. Send bytes, observe output
and wait for exit while the callback runs. A detached `ProgramResult` remains
usable after the scopes close; the interactive handle does not.

The [complete example](../examples/managed-program/Main.hs) runs a command,
cancels an observation, sends literal input, waits again and exercises an owning
deadline. Use the README's private demonstration server before running it.

<!-- example: managed-program -->
```haskell
{-# LANGUAGE OverloadedRecordDot #-}
{-# LANGUAGE OverloadedStrings #-}
{-# LANGUAGE TypeApplications #-}

module Main (main) where

import Control.Concurrent.Async (asyncThreadId, wait, withAsync)
import Control.Concurrent.MVar
import Control.Exception
import Control.Monad (unless)
import Data.ByteString.Char8 qualified as Bytes
import LibTmux qualified as Tmux
import LibTmux.Capabilities qualified as Cap
import LibTmux.Program qualified as Program
import System.Environment (getArgs)
import System.Exit (die)
import System.OsPath.Posix qualified as Path
import System.OsString.Posix qualified as Os

main :: IO ()
main = getArgs >>= \case
  [socketArgument, executableArgument] -> do
    socket <- Path.encodeFS socketArgument
    executable <- Path.encodeFS executableArgument
    let config = (Tmux.serverConfig socket) {Tmux.executable = executable}
    Tmux.withServer config $ \server -> do
      unless (Cap.supports (Tmux.serverCapabilities server) Cap.ManagedPrograms)
        (die "This example requires connected tmux 3.8 or newer")
      before <- Tmux.capture server
      result <- Tmux.runProgram server (settings "/bin/sh"
        ["-c", "printf '%s' \"$1\"; exit 7", "app", "literal ; $HOME"])
      require (result.programExit == Program.ProgramExited 7) "exit status changed"
      require ("literal ; $HOME" `Bytes.isPrefixOf` result.programOutput.screenBytes) "argv changed"
      putStrLn ("exit: " <> show result.programExit)
      putStrLn "literal argv: True"

      Tmux.withProgram server (settings "/bin/sh"
        ["-c", "IFS= read -r line; printf 'received:%s' \"$line\""]) $ \program -> do
          observing <- newEmptyMVar
          withAsync (try @AsyncException (putMVar observing () >> Program.waitProgram program)) $ \observer -> do
            takeMVar observing
            throwTo (asyncThreadId observer) ThreadKilled
            cancelled <- wait observer
            require (cancelled == Left ThreadKilled) "observation did not report cancellation"
          Program.sendProgramInput program "literal ; $HOME\n"
          Program.waitProgram program >>= \status -> require (status == Program.ProgramExited 0) "interactive exit changed"
          output <- Program.readProgramScreen program
          require ("received:literal ; $HOME" `Bytes.isInfixOf` output.screenBytes) "input changed"
      putStrLn "cancelled observation: True"
      putStrLn "interactive retry: True"

      entered <- newEmptyMVar
      expired <- try @Program.ProgramError (Tmux.withProgram server
        (settings "/bin/sh" ["-c", "trap '' HUP TERM; exec /bin/cat -"])
          {Program.executionTimeout = Just 0.5} $ \program ->
            putMVar entered () >> Program.waitProgram program)
      started <- tryTakeMVar entered
      require (started == Just () && expired == Left Program.ProgramTimedOut) "owning deadline did not clean up active work"
      putStrLn "owning deadline: True"
      after <- Tmux.capture server
      require (map (.ref) (Tmux.sessions before) == map (.ref) (Tmux.sessions after)
        && map (.ref) (Tmux.panes before) == map (.ref) (Tmux.panes after)) "borrowed resources changed"
      putStrLn "borrowed resources preserved: True"
  _ -> die "Usage: managed-program SOCKET TMUX_EXECUTABLE"

settings :: String -> [String] -> Program.ProgramOptions
settings file args = Program.programOptions (Os.fromBytestring (Bytes.pack file))
  (map (Os.fromBytestring . Bytes.pack) args)

require :: Bool -> String -> IO ()
require condition message = unless condition (die message)
```

## Check the connected daemon

`serverCapabilities` is a pure report from the daemon release accepted through
the Server's pinned socket. The client executable's release does not enable an
older daemon. `supports` and `requireCapability` use the same
[`capabilityRegistry`](../src/LibTmux/Capabilities.hs) as each operation.
[`capabilities.json`](../capabilities.json) is checked against that table.

The complete Program operations require released tmux 3.8. Older versions,
`next-3.8` and 3.8 release candidates refuse before application effects. Each
input, capture and exit operation has a separate registry entry because each
also depends on the generation witness established during startup. A dead pin
cannot route an operation to a replacement daemon.

This initial slice requires a local Linux daemon, process-group pidfd signaling
from Linux 6.9, procfs, and Bash dynamic descriptors and timed reads. Host
requirements are checked separately before creating an application. A private
bootstrap uses positional arguments, direct exec and the actual PTY. It neither
evaluates the executable and argv as shell syntax nor replaces application input
with a line-oriented protocol.

`bootstrapShell` selects Bash, defaulting to `/bin/bash`. The library probes
dynamic descriptors, a timed FIFO read, descriptor closure and `execfail` before
creating a session. Its FIFO opens read/write, so loss of the controller's
writer cannot block the open. The gate read has a separate one-second startup
lease; cleanup sends a blank claim to wake an admitted reader immediately.
`commandTimeout` bounds each native command. Neither bounds whole startup;
use `executionTimeout` for the owning setup and callback. The descriptor closes
before application exec. A delayed startup may refuse without executing the
application. Only GNU Bash 5.3.9 has been exercised
locally; these feature checks do not establish another Bash release's support.

## Configure argv and bounds

Import `LibTmux.Program` qualified for `ProgramOptions` record updates. Start
with `programOptions executable arguments`; an empty tail supports a
zero-argument executable. POSIX paths, argv and environment values retain
non-NUL bytes. A missing cwd and a failed exec have separate `ProgramStartFailed`
phases; normal application exit 127 is still `ProgramExited 127`.

| Option | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `workingDirectory` | Strict cwd, defaulting to the caller's current directory. |
| `environment` | Overrides the daemon's inherited application environment; the ownership token is reserved. |
| `bootstrapShell` | Absolute path to Bash; unavailable or incompatible binaries refuse before application creation. |
| `columns`, `rows` | Initial geometry, at most 500 by 200 cells. Capture refuses if an external resize changes it. |
| `historyLines` | At most 10000 lines and one million cells with the screen. |
| `outputLimit` | Rendered bytes returned, from one byte to 1 MiB. |
| `commandTimeout` | Positive per-command deadline, at most ten seconds. |
| `executionTimeout` | Optional owning setup/callback deadline with a separate cleanup budget. |

The combined argv, environment and cwd limit is 8192 bytes, with at most 4096
argv entries and 4096 environment entries. Invalid inputs refuse before
application creation. Options have no `Show` instance because they may contain
credentials.

Environment names are ASCII shell identifiers. `_`, `SHLVL`, `POSIXLY_CORRECT`,
`BASH_COMPAT`, `LIBTMUX_PROGRAM_TOKEN` and the `__libtmux_` prefix are reserved.
Readonly or otherwise unassignable Bash names refuse during the preflight.
Assignments apply after the ownership claim and strict cwd change, so tmux's
client-PATH substitution and bootstrap variables cannot alter the requested
application values.

## Observe and send input

| Operation | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `sendProgramInput` | At most 1024 literal bytes per call, including NUL. Terminal line discipline and echo still apply. Acceptance does not prove consumption. |
| `readProgramScreen` | A bounded rendered snapshot with retained history, `omittedBytes` for this snapshot and `historyTruncated` when earlier history may be lost. |
| `waitProgram` | The real leader exit or signal after tmux's final PTY drain. Signal text preserves tmux's name or decimal spelling. |
| `waitProgramFor` | Bounds observation and returns `Nothing` without stopping the program. |
| `terminateProgram` | TERM, up to 100ms for leader exit, then group KILL and the leader outcome. |

Window removal or adding another pane invalidates exit observation. A resize
of the single owned pane keeps its exit wait valid; capture still requires the
configured geometry. At most five native observers are registered at a time,
with their client and retained-byte costs charged to the existing Runtime.

Input and capture transfer a pending pane-generation witness in the same native
queue as the operation. An external respawn refuses the stale operation. An
uncertain submitted input is never replayed. Capture uses an owned named buffer
and bounded local spool; tmux hook stdout cannot become application output.
The native capture guard requires the configured geometry before allocating
its buffer. An external resize raises a mutation refusal; owning cleanup still
works. The selected history and screen cover at most one million cells, with
at most 32 bytes per cell in released tmux 3.8. Returned bytes have the separate
`outputLimit` bound. stdout and stderr share the PTY. Capture may clip bytes
inside a UTF-8 sequence; the result is a `ByteString` with an exact omission
count.

## Cancel and recover

Cancelling a wait leaves its owner running. Cancelling the owning scope or
setting `executionTimeout` initiates cleanup before returning. Async exceptions
keep their original class. Cleanup sends signals only through the retained
identity-bound pidfd; it never reacquires a numeric PGID.

Completed cleanup proves leader exit and an empty retained process group.
Zombies, uninterruptible members, changed tmux ownership or failed cleanup may
leave an incomplete owner. Processes that create a new group or session escape
this contract. A scope does not claim exhaustive process-tree accounting.

Catch exceptions with their `ExceptionContext` when cleanup must be retried.
`programRecoveries` retrieves `ProgramRecovery` owners;
`programCleanupFailure` retains the cleanup cause alongside the original body
exception. `inspectProgramCleanup` reads local metadata without tmux IO.
`resumeProgramCleanup` retries through the retained pin and native Runtime,
including after the borrowing Server has closed. It never relaunches an
application or replays input. External replacements remain untouched; a lost
witness may require the external owner to remove its resource before retry.

The initial precreation witness conservatively observes respawns throughout the
daemon until exact pane identity is available. An unrelated respawn during that
short interval can refuse startup. Raw byte streaming, readiness predicates,
controller-crash leases, keep/detach and MCP are not implemented.

# Rename captured targets

[`renameSession`](../src/LibTmux/Server.hs),
[`renameWindow`](../src/LibTmux/Server.hs) and
[`setPaneTitle`](../src/LibTmux/Server.hs) act in `IO` on opaque references
from the same [`Server`](../src/LibTmux/Server.hs). Renaming a window changes
the physical window everywhere it is linked, not one session slot.

The program validates every selection before its first mutation. It changes the
server you give it, so use the [README's demo server](../README.md). Run from a
[checkout](../.github/CONTRIBUTING.md#toolchain):

```console
$ cabal run --verbose=0 mutate-graph -- \
    "$LIBTMUX_DEMO_DIR/s" \
    "$(command -v tmux)"
```

- The session rename, window rename and title change are separate commands. A
  later failure does not undo earlier ones.
- Afterward, run the README's cleanup commands. The program leaves the daemon
  running.

<!-- example: mutate-graph -->
```haskell
{-# LANGUAGE OverloadedRecordDot #-}
{-# LANGUAGE OverloadedStrings #-}

-- | Rename a session and a window, set a pane title, then show the state
-- before and after.
module Main (main) where

import Control.Exception (rethrowIO)
import Data.Function ((&))
import Data.Text qualified as Text
import LibTmux qualified as Tmux
import LibTmux.Query qualified as Q
import LibTmux.Query.Pane qualified as Pane
import System.Environment (getArgs)
import System.Exit (die)
import System.OsPath.Posix qualified as Path

main :: IO ()
main = getArgs >>= \case
  [socketArgument, executableArgument] -> do
    socket <- Path.encodeFS socketArgument
    executable <- Path.encodeFS executableArgument
    let config = (Tmux.serverConfig socket) {Tmux.executable = executable}
        selected = Q.panes & Q.matching (Q.eq Pane.active True)
    result <- Tmux.tryTmux $ Tmux.withServer config $ \server -> do
      before <- Tmux.capture server
      session <- require "Session selection"
        (Q.exactlyOne (Tmux.sessions before))
      matches <- require "Pane query" (Q.runQuery before selected)
      pane <- require "Pane selection" (Q.exactlyOne matches)
      window <- require "Pane's window" (Tmux.lookupWindow before pane.window)

      Tmux.renameSession server session.ref "workspace"
      Tmux.renameWindow server window.ref "api #{pid};"
      Tmux.setPaneTitle server pane.ref "editor-ready"
      after <- Tmux.capture server
      pure (before, after, session, window, pane)
    case result of
      Left problem -> rethrowIO problem
      Right (before, after, session, window, pane) -> do
        changedSession <- require "Fresh session"
          (Tmux.lookupSession after session.ref)
        changedWindow <- require "Fresh window"
          (Tmux.lookupWindow after window.ref)
        changedPane <- require "Fresh pane" (Tmux.lookupPane after pane.ref)
        oldWindow <- require "Old window" (Tmux.lookupWindow before window.ref)
        oldName <- require "Old window encoding" (Tmux.labelText oldWindow.name)
        newName <- require "New window encoding"
          (Tmux.labelText changedWindow.name)
        let links =
              [link | link <- Tmux.windowLinks after, link.window == window.ref]
        putStrLn $ "session: " <> Text.unpack session.name <> " -> "
          <> Text.unpack changedSession.name
        putStrLn $ "window: " <> Text.unpack oldName <> " -> "
          <> Text.unpack newName
        putStrLn $ "pane title: " <> Text.unpack changedPane.title
        putStrLn $ "physical window links: " <> show (length links)
        putStrLn $ "same target identities: " <> show
          (session.ref == changedSession.ref
            && window.ref == changedWindow.ref
            && pane.ref == changedPane.ref)
        putStrLn $ "old snapshot values: " <> Text.unpack session.name <> ", "
          <> Text.unpack oldName
  _ -> die "Usage: mutate-graph SOCKET TMUX_EXECUTABLE"

require :: Show problem => String -> Either problem a -> IO a
require context = either (die . ((context <> ": ") <>) . show) pure
```

## Send input to a pane

[`sendKeys`](../src/LibTmux/Server.hs) takes an exact `PaneRef` and
`PaneInput`. Pass `LiteralText "Enter"` to type the five characters.
`NamedKeys ("Enter" :| [])` sends one key. The
[creation example](creation.md) shows both requests to a newly created pane.

Import `(:|)` from `Data.List.NonEmpty` for a named key sequence. tmux
checks every name before the library sends the sequence. An invalid name
raises `InvalidMutationArgument` before any keys are sent. Use
`sendKeysWith` to set one deadline for validation and sending.

Success confirms that tmux processed the input request. Observe the pane
separately when your program needs evidence that the application responded.

## Read pane text

[`capturePane`](../src/LibTmux/Server.hs) takes an exact pane reference.
Start with `defaultPaneCapture` for the visible rows in plain Unicode.
Use `paneText` to read the captured text. The
[creation example](creation.md) captures its own pane.

Set `rows` to `RowsBetween (-10) (-1)` for ten rows before the first
visible row. Offsets are inclusive and accepted from -2147483647 through
32767. tmux clamps them to the rows it retained. Set `rendering` to `AnsiStyled` to keep tmux's color and
style escapes. Empty rows remain in either format.

The byte limit applies before UTF-8 decoding. An oversized capture raises
`PaneTextTooLarge` instead of returning clipped text. The transport limit
also covers the enclosing reply and any hook output.
An after-hook failure raises `PaneCaptureHookFailed` with its diagnostic.

## Wait for pane text

[`waitForText`](../src/LibTmux/Server.hs) looks for a case-sensitive substring.
With `defaultPaneWait`, the first visible match is enough and the deadline
is one second.

For a fresh match, take a `capturePane` baseline before input and set
`waitMatch = FreshSince baseline`. Use the same pane, row range and rendering.
The wait needs either observed absence followed by presence or an additional
occurrence. Moving an old prompt or repainting it in place supplies no new
evidence. Pick a marker the application prints so ordinary terminal echo
cannot satisfy the wait. The [complete example](creation.md) disables echo
and observes its own process.

The result is `PaneTextMatched`, `PaneTextTimedOut` or `PaneTextExited`.
A timeout or exit carries the last complete capture when available. A timeout
during a capture can also carry a [recovery owner](#keep-recovery-ownership-reachable).
The first capture runs immediately. After a nonmatch, the library checks the
pane and waits up to 100 ms before reading again. One deadline bounds all these
steps.

## Read and change the environment

[`getEnvironment`](../src/LibTmux/Server.hs) looks up a name in
`GlobalEnvironment` or `SessionEnvironment session`. A session lookup reads
that table directly. A missing name returns `Nothing`. A missing session
raises `EnvironmentReadRejected`.

[`setEnvironment`](../src/LibTmux/Server.hs) stores literal bytes with
`Visible` or `Hidden` visibility. Hidden entries stay in tmux and are omitted
when it starts a process. Names must be nonempty and cannot contain NUL or
`=`. Values cannot contain NUL. Values can contain newlines and invalid UTF-8.

Use [`markEnvironmentRemoved`](../src/LibTmux/Server.hs) to mask a value
that a new process would otherwise inherit. Use
[`unsetEnvironment`](../src/LibTmux/Server.hs) to delete the entry from
the selected table. The [creation example](creation.md) observes an empty
value, a removal marker and an absent entry.

## Targets, names and deadlines

- A reference from another connection generation, or from an
  [offline fixture](fixtures.md), fails with `InvalidTarget` before dispatch.
- A closed handle fails with `ServerClosed`.
- A reference does not prove the target still exists; tmux can reject one
  deleted since capture. Select the intended entity first with
  [typed queries](query.md).

Names:

- Window names are [`TmuxText`](../src/LibTmux/Snapshot.hs): bytes, with an
  explicit conversion to text that can fail. String literals work with
  [OverloadedStrings](https://downloads.haskell.org/ghc/latest/docs/users_guide/exts/overloaded_strings.html);
  `labelFromBytes` takes bytes.
- Session names and pane titles are
  [`Text`](https://hackage-content.haskell.org/package/text-2.1.3/docs/Data-Text.html#t:Text).
- tmux may reject a name its release does not accept.
- NUL and encoded command arguments over 16,364 bytes fail before dispatch.
  The limit includes terminators, format expansion and escaped separators.
- The pane's application can replace a title later.

Deadlines:

- Default: one second, covering submission and waiting for the response.
- Forms such as [`renameWindowWith`](../src/LibTmux/Server.hs) take
  [`MutationOptions`](../src/LibTmux/Server.hs) first, for example
  `Tmux.defaultMutationOptions {Tmux.timeout = 2}`.
- Timeouts must be positive, up to ten seconds. They bound the wait, not
  configured hooks.
- Nothing retries automatically.

## Known and uncertain outcomes

[`tryTmux`](../src/LibTmux/Server.hs) catches library operational exceptions
with their context. It lets application exceptions and asynchronous
cancellation propagate.

- `MutationRejected` means tmux rejected the primary command.
- `MutationAppliedWithErrors` means the primary command ran and a later hook
  failed. The failure does not imply rollback.
- `MutationTimedOut` means the caller deadline elapsed. It does not establish
  whether the command ran. Inspect the correlated status before deciding what
  responsibility remains.

Use the exception constructor to distinguish rejection from an applied hook
error; both have a completed `Failed` operation status. A successful response
does not establish that background jobs started by a hook have finished.

## Keep recovery ownership reachable

Read [`mutationRecoveries`](../src/LibTmux/Server.hs) from the exception
context that `tryTmux` or
[`Control.Exception.tryWithContext`](https://hackage-content.haskell.org/package/base-4.22.0.0/docs/Control-Exception.html#v:tryWithContext)
returns.

- Each owner has a `mutationOperation` and `mutationGeneration`.
- Its receipt keeps metadata, not the command operands or result.
- An operation that was never admitted has no owner.

Then:

- [`inspectMutationRecovery`](../src/LibTmux/Server.hs) reads the status and
  native ownership locally.
- `resumeMutationRecovery` resumes cleanup without resending the command.
- `awaitMutationRecovery` waits for the local owners to retire. If cleanup may
  need resuming, inspect first. Cancelling the wait keeps the owner.
- `detachMutationRecovery` gives up the remaining responsibility. Decide who
  owns it first: detaching does not stop daemon work, release native resources
  or repeat the mutation.

An exited native child does not turn `OutcomeUnknown` into success, and
retained uncertainty can hold later commands back. After a callback or scope
cleanup fails, see [shared Runtime](shared-runtime.md).

Not implemented yet: creation, pane input, contextual window operations and
event streams; see [status](status.md).

# Share a Runtime across independent Server scopes

[`withRuntime`](../src/LibTmux/Server.hs) gives several components one
resource and cleanup owner. Open each endpoint with
[`withServerIn`](../src/LibTmux/Server.hs). Closing one Server scope releases
only that handle; the others keep working under the shared limits.

Start the [demo server](../README.md) from the README, then run from a
checkout:

```console
$ cabal run --verbose=0 shared-runtime -- \
    "$LIBTMUX_DEMO_DIR/s" \
    "$(command -v tmux)"
```

<!-- example: shared-runtime -->
```haskell
{-# LANGUAGE OverloadedRecordDot #-}

-- | Share Runtime resources while keeping Server lifetimes independent.
module Main (main) where

import Control.Exception (ExceptionWithContext (..))
import Control.Monad (forM_, unless)
import Data.Text qualified as Text
import LibTmux qualified as Tmux
import System.Environment (getArgs)
import System.Exit (die)
import System.OsPath.Posix qualified as Path

main :: IO ()
main = getArgs >>= \case
  [socketArgument, executableArgument] -> do
    socket <- Path.encodeFS socketArgument
    executable <- Path.encodeFS executableArgument
    let config = (Tmux.serverConfig socket) {Tmux.executable = executable}
    snapshot <- Tmux.withRuntime $ \runtime ->
      Tmux.withServerIn runtime config $ \outer -> do
        first <- Tmux.capture outer
        closed <- Tmux.withServerIn runtime config $ \inner -> do
          unless (Tmux.serverGeneration inner /= Tmux.serverGeneration outer) $
            fail "independent handles shared a connection generation"
          captured <- Tmux.capture inner
          case Tmux.panes captured of
            pane : _ -> unless (Tmux.lookupPane first pane.ref == Left Tmux.ForeignGeneration) $
              fail "a reference crossed independent handle generations"
            [] -> fail "the owned example fixture has no pane"
          pure inner
        Tmux.tryTmux (Tmux.capture closed) >>= \case
          Left (ExceptionWithContext _ Tmux.ServerClosed) -> pure ()
          Left problem -> fail ("closed handle returned an unexpected error: " <> show problem)
          Right _ -> fail "the inner handle remained open after its scope"
        Tmux.capture outer
    putStrLn "independent handles: verified"
    putStrLn "closed inner handle: rejected"
    putStrLn $ "outer capture panes: " <> show (length (Tmux.panes snapshot))
    forM_ (Tmux.panes snapshot) $ \pane -> do
      window <- either (fail . show) pure (Tmux.lookupWindow snapshot pane.window)
      putStrLn $ "detached pane " <> Text.unpack (Tmux.renderPaneId (Tmux.paneId pane.ref))
        <> " belongs to " <> Text.unpack (Tmux.renderWindowId (Tmux.windowId window.ref))
  _ -> die "Usage: shared-runtime SOCKET TMUX_EXECUTABLE"
```

The program checks that:

- References stay connection-scoped.
- The inner handle closes.
- The outer handle still captures.
- Detached navigation works after the whole Runtime closes.

```text
detached pane %0 belongs to @0
```

## Scope and recovery

- Every adoption has its own generation, even for the same daemon. A reference
  from one handle does not target another handle's observations.
- Closing the Runtime also closes handles that application tasks still hold.
  You own your worker lifetimes.
- Adopting after the Runtime closes raises `RuntimeClosed`.
- Closing either kind of scope leaves the tmux daemon running.

Limits belong to the Runtime:

- It admits one complete capture at a time. A concurrent attempt can fail with
  an operational capacity error.
- Capture sequentially, or use separate Runtimes for separate capacity. See
  [performance](performance.md) for the measured workload.

Recovery:

- Catch with [`tryTmux`](../src/LibTmux/Server.hs) to keep the exception
  context. `cleanupRecoveries` returns the remaining cleanup owners.
- Inspect, retry, wait and detach act on the one responsibility you select.
- A failed adoption can hold an owner before it returns a Server. Recovering it
  does not close neighboring handles.
- Nested scopes can contribute overlapping owners. Inspect and resume each.
- An explicit cleanup wait has no deadline. Cancelling it keeps the owner.
- Detaching releases no native resource and proves no daemon-side completion.

More: [capture recovery](capture.md#errors-and-recovery) and the
[process contract](contracts/process.md#public-scope-outcomes) for the error and
cancellation policy.


<!-- example: offline-graph -->
```haskell
{-# LANGUAGE OverloadedRecordDot #-}
{-# LANGUAGE OverloadedStrings #-}

-- | Test a pane-selection policy without starting tmux or opening a socket.
module Main (main) where

import Data.Bifunctor (first)
import LibTmux qualified as Tmux
import LibTmux.Snapshot.Fixture qualified as F
import System.Exit (die)
import System.OsString.Posix qualified as Os

main :: IO ()
main = do
  snapshot <- either die pure buildSnapshot
  print (Tmux.snapshotOrigin snapshot)
  print
    [ (Tmux.renderPaneId (Tmux.paneId pane.ref), Tmux.dimensionValue pane.width)
    | pane <- Tmux.panes snapshot
    , pane.active
    , Tmux.dimensionValue pane.width >= 120
    ]
  print (length (Tmux.windows snapshot), length (Tmux.paneOccurrences snapshot))

buildSnapshot :: Either String Tmux.Snapshot
buildSnapshot = do
  version <- checked (Tmux.parseVersion "3.8")
  sid <- checked (Tmux.parseSessionId "$1")
  wid <- checked (Tmux.parseWindowId "@2")
  pid <- checked (Tmux.parsePaneId "%3")
  width <- checked (Tmux.mkDimension 120)
  height <- checked (Tmux.mkDimension 40)
  paneIndex <- checked (Tmux.mkPaneIndex 0)
  firstIndex <- checked (Tmux.mkWindowIndex 0)
  secondIndex <- checked (Tmux.mkWindowIndex 4)
  let origin = F.fixtureOrigin "reports"
      session = Tmux.Session (F.sessionRef origin sid) "work" 0
      window = Tmux.Window (F.windowRef origin wid) "editor" width height
      pane = Tmux.Pane
        { Tmux.ref = F.paneRef origin pid
        , Tmux.window = window.ref
        , Tmux.index = paneIndex
        , Tmux.width = width
        , Tmux.height = height
        , Tmux.active = True
        , Tmux.dead = False
        , Tmux.title = "editor"
        , Tmux.currentCommand = Os.fromBytestring "ghci"
        , Tmux.currentPath = Os.fromBytestring "/offline/project"
        }
      input = (F.emptyFixture origin version)
        { F.sessions = [session], F.windows = [window], F.panes = [pane]
        , F.windowLinks = [Tmux.WindowLink session.ref firstIndex window.ref True,
                          Tmux.WindowLink session.ref secondIndex window.ref False]
        }
  checked (F.validateFixture origin input)

checked :: Show problem => Either problem value -> Either String value
checked = first show
```

Program output:

<!-- example-output: offline-graph -->
```text
DefinedOffline "reports"
[("%3",120)]
(1,2)
```

- `fixtureOrigin` creates a named offline namespace. Reuse a name for
  successive observations in one test scenario; use different names for
  independent scenarios.
- Fixture references never equal references from an adopted Server, even when
  the native IDs match.

Building a fixture:

- `emptyFixture` supplies synthetic server metadata and empty collections. Fill
  in ordinary records, then call `validateFixture`.
- Validation covers reference membership, duplicate slots, active selections
  and attached-client context. A bad input returns `FixtureError`, never an
  empty snapshot.
- Editing a record does not validate the graph or update a snapshot already
  built.
- Live acquisition applies wire decoding, tmux's field normalization and
  transport limits. Fixtures can build cases a live capture cannot produce.

Provenance:

- `SnapshotOrigin` distinguishes `DefinedOffline` from `AcquiredFromTmux`.
  Offline snapshots have no acquisition interval.
- Neither provenance nor an opaque reference proves a tmux target is alive.

For observations acquired from tmux, see [capture and recovery](capture.md).

## IDs and indices describe different things

- [`SessionId`](../src/LibTmux/Id.hs) (`$`), [`WindowId`](../src/LibTmux/Id.hs)
  (`@`) and [`PaneId`](../src/LibTmux/Id.hs) (`%`) are distinct types.
- Parsers require the prefix, canonical decimal spelling and an unsigned 32-bit
  value. Leading zeroes and whitespace fail.
- Use the rendering functions to produce target text for tmux.
- An ID carries no endpoint or server lifetime. Parsing `@17` does not prove the
  window exists.
- Generation-bound references come from a validated [snapshot](capture.md).

Indices:

- [`WindowIndex`](../src/LibTmux/Value.hs): a window link's position in its
  session.
- [`PaneIndex`](../src/LibTmux/Value.hs): a pane's position in its window.
- Neither is an entity ID. A physical window can have several links, even at
  several indices in one session.

## Validate values where they enter the program

- Constructors return `Either`: dimensions must be positive, indices
  nonnegative.
- Numeric accessors return `Integer`, so reading a value never narrows it to a
  machine-sized integer.
- [`mkDimension`](../src/LibTmux/Value.hs) checks the mathematical domain. A
  tmux command can impose a smaller range; a valid dimension does not promise
  that command's maximum.

## Release admission has a limited meaning

- [`parseVersion`](../src/LibTmux/Version.hs) accepts the spellings tmux
  reports in the output format of `tmux -V`, including one final LF: `X.Y`,
  `X.Ya`, `X.Y-rc`, `X.Y-rcN` and `next-X.Y`. They rank
  `next-X.Y < X.Y-rc < X.Y-rcN < X.Y < X.Ya`, with numeric components compared
  as numbers. A bare `master`, unknown suffixes and trailing data fail.
- [`requireSupported`](../src/LibTmux/Version.hs) admits tmux 3.3a and every
  newer release, with no upper bound. Plain 3.3 and older releases fail. A
  development build or candidate passes when it ranks above 3.3a.
- Both check the release identity you supply. They do not inspect the host,
  vouch for every feature of that release, or show that the project tested it.
